search_topic: predicting future egocentric gridworld frames from actions (learned world model, next-frame prediction)
brief: a world model (`world_model.py`, function predict) that rolls out 24 future 5x5 egocentric frames of an 11x11 gridworld with two switches and two lamps (hidden switch-to-lamp wiring) from 16 context frames and the future actions; the horizon revisits 8 context moves, then takes 16 fresh actions into possibly unseen cells. loss = 1 - fraction of exactly correct frames on 200 dev episodes; a further 200 fresh-seed episodes are graded once after the run, so generalize rather than fit the dev seeds. Public examples are in data/train.jsonl and env.py must not be imported
proxy_note: synthetic proxy, not PlayWorld; harder variant with held-out fresh seeds and no published reference
